newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate to hold June fast track trade hearings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate to hold June fast track trade hearings.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee chairman William Roth Tuesday announced hearings in early June on renewal of fast track trade negotiating authority.

Roth, a Delaware Republican, said he agreed to hold the hearings after receiving assurance from U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky that President Clinton would actively work for passage of fast track authority.

"As I told Ambassador Barshefsky, fast track will be renewed only if it gains the support of a bipartisan majority. I stand ready to do what I can ... to help create that bipartisan majority," he said in a statement.

Roth said fast track authority should be renewed quickly to permit the Clinton administration to negotiate trade agreements with Latin America and open markets in Asia. "I am particularly concerned that the delays in renewing fast track leave us unable to forge new trade agreements," he said.
"Ambassador Barshefsky assured me that President Clinton would be as involved in passage of fast track as he was in passage of the NAFTA agreement (North American Free Trade Agreement)," Roth added.

Clinton said during a trip last week to Mexico, Costa Rica and Barbados said that he wants fast track authority to pass Congress this year, but that the first order of business would be to pass the balanced budget program.
Fast track is a term that refers to a special, faster procedure for Congress to consider legislation which puts in place trade agreements.

Under this procedure, the administration consults closely with Congress during the negotiations but once the agreement is presented to Congress, only a limited time is available for either approval without change or rejection.
The proposed legislation has been delayed over a dispute between Republicans and Democrats over whether it should include authority to negotiate labor and environment issues.
Roth said he told the administration that to win bipartisan support for fast track it must ease Republican concerns on labor and environment issues.
But many key Congressional Democrats, backed by labor and environmental groups, have said that they will not support fast track authority that does not include labor and environment.
